To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the placenta is the major source of fetal ASP in pregnancy; 2) the placenta produces ASP in response to insulin, and this response is enhanced by maternal obesity.
elevated fetal adipsin (ASP) in maternal serum of obese pregnant women is due to placental ASP secretion, and this placental ASP secretion occurs via Hofbauer (HB) cells.
elevated ASP in obese pregnancy is associated with increased placental expression of ASP, which is mediated via the placental macrophage, the Hofbauer cell.

the role of the placenta in fetal programming and the role of ASP in the pathogenesis of metabolic syndrome.

the elevated adipsin/ASP in obesity is not of fetal origin, but is secreted by the placenta.
